Root cause identified this turn for the pointer-drag inconclusiveness: mouse.down/move/up drag gestures do not register ANY weight change under this Playwright/headless-Chromium harness (confirmed 3x across two review turns and two distinct gesture patterns -- grownWeightChanged stayed exactly 29/29 every time), most likely a setPointerCapture-retargeting quirk of CDP-dispatched synthetic pointer events rather than a real app defect; this also means review-4's own maxRatioDrift:0.0 pro-rata confirmation and BHV-30's sum-invariant confirmation were measured against a no-op, not a real edit, and should not be relied on as positive evidence of those specific claims. implementer.notes: claude-code/sonnet-5 (remediation turn, F10). Two independent, root-caused defects, not one -- direct Chromium launch, own build/server, 5x repeated live measurement for stability. (1) Measurement geometry: review-5-ring-alpha-v2.mjs assumed the ring's overview projection is a circle centred on the sun; the overview camera is oblique (cameraForOverview: elevated, forward-offset, not top-down), so a flat ring projects as an ELLIPSE -- the assumed-circle far point can miss the true ring band entirely (confirmed: CBRS's assumed far point fell 192px off-canvas from its true camera-projected position). Fixed by adding planet.label.dataset.ringFarArc (OrreryScene.tsx): a 5-point arc of EXACT 3D far-side points run through the real per-frame camera projection every frame, no circle assumed; reference point is the same far point offset 40px radially outward from the sun in screen space (a larger 3D-radius reference was tried first and rejected -- it drifted across the scene's own radial background vignette for outer rings, reading as signal unrelated to the ring). With ONLY this fix, the far side still read at background level (delta ~2, both rings) -- ruling out 'it was only a measurement bug' and confirming F10's original finding was substantively correct. (2) Two real rendering defects, isolated with a direct visibility/alpha/color stress test (forced aAlpha=1, uColor=magenta -- full ellipse rendered correctly, proving the mesh/geometry/shader pipeline itself was sound) then reintroducing real values one variable at a time: (a) OVERVIEW_RING_ALPHA.floor (0.22) is genuinely below the perceptibility threshold at this ring color (#66756f) and background/exposure -- confirmed even the PEAK value (0.55) applied uniformly still failed to clear the >6 delta gate (ASML delta 1.72, CBRS delta 2.79), so this was never just a floor-vs-peak question. (b) ringDescriptor.widthPx (the intended on-screen ring width, 1.5px) was computed in scene-model.ts but never consumed by the renderer -- the ring mesh used a FIXED 3D half-width (0.012) regardless of orbitRadius; under this perspective camera a fixed 3D width projects to progressively fewer screen pixels as orbitRadius (and so camera distance) grows, causing sub-pixel anti-aliased dropout for outer rings independent of alpha (confirmed: CBRS stayed undetectable even at alpha 1.0 with the old fixed width). Fixed by computing the 3D half-width from ringDescriptor.widthPx and this ring's own farthest camera distance (sampled at 32 points around the full circle, so the worst-case/far-side point is guaranteed at least widthPx screen pixels wide, same pinhole relationship the file already uses for planet/label projection) -- OrreryScene.tsx, ring construction. Both levers were then re-tuned together empirically (peak/floor raised from 0.55/0.22 to 0.85/0.7 -- still a genuine token PAIR with a real falloff, not a single constant; widthPx raised from 1.5 to 4) against 5 repeated live measurements until both sampled rings (smallest and largest on-canvas orbit) cleared the unweakened >6 delta threshold with comfortable, repeatable margin: ASML 17.0-18.0, CBRS 10.7-19.5 across 5 runs, allSampledRingsVisibleAboveBackground true every run.
